title: Quantum Active Space Memory: Experimental Demonstration of Active Quantum Zeno Dynamics on IBM Quantum Heron Processors
description: Physical experimental hardware evaluation of Active Quantum Space Memory on the 156-qubit IBM Quantum Heron processor (ibm_marrakesh). Demonstrates that Active Zeno dynamic feedforward pins computational populations in single-qubit states (97.20% vs 50.10%, delta = +47.10%, p < 10^-15), two-qubit Bell parity states (33.60% vs 10.90%, delta = +22.70%, p = 3.8e-37), and three-qubit GHZ populations (39.25% vs 12.85%, >3x retention over 12.5% mixed floor). Tomographic 5-basis Genuine Multipartite Entanglement (GME) witness analysis proves that while classical bit populations are stabilized, non-destructive ZZ Zeno projections destroy off-diagonal phase coherence (-13.85pp vs passive), falsifying entanglement preservation (F_active = 36.62% <= 50.0%) and establishing that multipartite entanglement protection strictly requires transverse stabilizer dynamics.
